terminology: joint response-threshold domain, not a code-compliant statutory safety domain
reason: The frozen 100 m numerical benchmark is not tied to a specified pipe grade, design class, code, or project safety factor. Its axial-stress increments are far below ordinary steel strength limits; adopting a material strength value would make stress non-controlling throughout the registered domain. Three explicit operational threshold scenarios are therefore used to test the valve-closure workflow without claiming regulatory compliance.

source_model.selection_basis: non-oracle physics-event sampling and sealed 24-case comparison

minimum_closure_rule: smallest scanned closure ratio for which the selected case and every slower closure on the registered scan satisfy all three thresholds
dominant_control_rule: largest utilization among pressure increment, axial-stress increment, and minimum-pressure lower-bound utilization; top-two difference <= 0.03 is reported as joint control

boundary_moc_registration.selection: deterministic maximin subset among cases with nominal maximum utilization closest to one, stratified by dominant control and safe/unsafe side

claim_limits: Thresholds are illustrative operational constraints and are not extracted from a design code.
No conclusion is permitted outside the registered three-parameter domain.
Boundary cases require new high-resolution MOC confirmation before reporting false-safe statistics.
A real project application must replace the three threshold scenarios with project-specific allowable values and safety factors.
